instructions.primary_message: Place yeast and warm water (105° F - 115° F) in a large mixing bowl; whisk to combine and set aside to hydrate, about 5 minutes. (Alternatively, you can place them in the bowl of a stand mixer.)

Meanwhile, cut butter into small pieces and place in a small saucepan along with the milk. Place the pan over medium-low and heat, stirring often, until butter is just melted and milk is lightly warm to the touch (105°F - 115°F). Remove from heat.
instructions.secondary_message:
5 tbsp butter, unsalted
237 ml whole milk

instructions.primary_message: Add the warm milk mixture, egg, sugar, and salt to the bowl with the hydrated yeast; whisk to combine.
instructions.secondary_message:
1 egg
3 tbsp granulated sugar
1 tsp salt

instructions.primary_message: Gradually add bread flour to the bowl, mixing by hand, until combined. (Alternatively, if using a stand mixer with dough hook attachment, mix on low speed until combined, about 1 minute.)

Gradually add 1 ½ cups all-purpose flour to the bowl, mixing by hand, until combined. (Alternatively, if using a stand mixer with dough hook attachment, mix on low speed until combined, 1 minute more.)
Add additional all-purpose flour to the bowl, a few tablespoons at a time, to create a dough that is moist but not sticky to the touch. (You may not need the full ½-cup of additional flour.)
Knead the dough by hand, until smooth and elastic, about 10 minutes. (Alternatively, if using a stand mixer, mix on medium-low speed until dough is smooth and elastic, 5-8 minutes.)
Place a large piece of plastic wrap on a flat surface; coat the top with a thin layer of oil.
instructions.secondary_message: ½ tsp extra virgin olive oil

instructions.primary_message: Remove dough from the bowl and place on top of the oiled plastic wrap. Add additional oil to the bowl used for the dough and spread to coat the inside. Return dough to the bowl and turn it over once to coat with oil. Loosely cover the bowl with the plastic wrap, oil-side facing down. Set the bowl in a warm place (70°F – 80°F), until dough has doubled in volume, 1 – 1 ½ hours.
instructions.secondary_message: ½ tsp extra virgin olive oil

instructions.primary_message: Once the dough has doubled, remove the plastic wrap (reserving it for later use), and press the dough down with your hands to release the air.
Coat a large (9 x 13-inch) baking dish with a thin layer of butter.

Divide the dough into 12 equal-sized pieces. On an unfloured surface, roll each piece of dough into a ball. Place the dough balls in the prepared baking dish, arranging them in three rows of four, with equal space in between. Loosely cover the rolls with the reserved plastic wrap, oil-side facing down. Set the bowl in a warm place (70°F – 80°F), until rolls have doubled in volume, about 1 hour.
About 15 minutes before the rolls are ready, preheat the oven to 425°F.
Place additional butter in a small saucepan and melt over low heat; set aside.

Once the rolls have doubled in volume, remove the plastic wrap and discard. Using a pastry brush, gently brush the top of the rolls with half of the melted butter (reserve remaining butter for when the rolls are done baking).
Place rolls in the oven and bake, undisturbed, until golden brown, about 15 minutes. Remove from the oven and brush with remaining melted butter. Set aside to cool.
Once the rolls are cool, remove from the baking dish and tear apart.
